facts.text: A pedestrian is any person on foot near a working machine; a spotter is a person assigned to stand where the operator can see them and guide a reversing or maneuvering machine using hand signals or radio.
facts.quote: A pedestrian is any person on foot near a working machine, and a spotter is a person whose job is to stand where the operator can see them and guide a reversing or maneuvering machine by hand signals or radio.

facts.text: Job-site pedestrians include ground crew, surveyors, mechanics, blast crews, supervisors and visitors.
facts.quote: On a job site "pedestrian" means ground crew, surveyors, mechanics, blast crews, supervisors and visitors.

facts.text: People on foot are the most vulnerable targets a working machine can hit and are often deliberately close to the machine.
facts.quote: They are the most vulnerable things a machine can hit, and they are often close on purpose.

facts.text: US rules accept an observer as an alternative to a reverse alarm, making the spotter a formal role.
facts.quote: A spotter is a formal role: US rules accept an observer as an alternative to a reverse alarm [Chapter 3]

facts.text: Queensland requires an authorized pedestrian approaching a machine to communicate with the operator and have that communication confirmed.
facts.quote: Queensland requires an authorized pedestrian approaching a machine to communicate with the operator and have that communication confirmed [Chapter 4]

facts.text: People on foot dominate the deaths described as clearly addressable by the collision mitigation system.
facts.quote: People on foot dominate the clearly addressable deaths

facts.text: People behind reversing machines accounted for 67% of 22 US surface-mine blind-area deaths.
facts.quote: 67% of 22 US surface-mine blind-area deaths were people behind reversing machines

facts.text: Underground, 39 miners were struck or pinned by continuous mining machines from 1984 to 2015.
facts.quote: underground, 39 miners were struck or pinned by continuous mining machines from 1984 to 2015 [Chapter 4]

facts.text: Mechanics remove wearable tags to work inside the danger zone, creating a design problem for tag-based proximity systems.
facts.quote: Mechanics remove wearable tags to work inside the danger zone

facts.text: An untagged contractor is invisible to a tag-based system.
facts.quote: an untagged contractor is invisible to a tag-based system [Chapter 4]

facts.text: A system applying the same exclusion zone to a walking worker, an authorized spotter and an intruder will either stop work constantly or require a controlled task-and-mode concept.
facts.quote: A system that applies the same exclusion zone to a walking worker, an authorized spotter and an intruder will either stop work constantly or need a controlled task-and-mode concept [Chapter 4].

facts.text: On-road pedestrian detection remains weak at night.
facts.quote: On the road, pedestrian detection remains weak at night

facts.text: In a 2025 on-road test, high-visibility clothing caused complete loss of pedestrian detection in some systems.
facts.quote: in a 2025 test high-visibility clothing caused a complete loss of detection in some systems [Chapter 10]

facts.text: Protecting people on foot is the main purpose of the collision mitigation system.
facts.quote: Protecting people on foot is the main purpose of the system

facts.text: Legitimate close work by ground crew makes collision mitigation detection zones difficult to design.
facts.quote: legitimate close work by ground crew is what makes the detection zones so hard to design [Chapter 4].
